spatial_claims.claim: SA, SB are similar and similarly situated parallelepipedal solids described on lines A, B respectively
SC, SD are similar and similarly situated parallelepipedal solids described on lines C, D respectively
SA:SB is the triplicate ratio of A:B (by 11.33 for similar parallelepipedal solids)
SC:SD is the triplicate ratio of C:D (by 11.33 for similar parallelepipedal solids)
SE is a parallelepipedal solid on E, similar and similarly situated to SC (constructed by 11.27)
SE = SC (equal solids, since both have the same ratio to SD)
If E > C then SE > SC for similar solids (by 11.33 and triplicate ratio)
If E < C then SC > SE for similar solids (by 11.33 and triplicate ratio)

configuration_map: The proof treats four straight lines A, B, C, D as magnitudes (lengths) in proportion A:B :: C:D. Parallelepipedal solids SA, SB, SC, SD are described on these lines but are never spatially analyzed — they are used only through their ratio properties via Proposition 11.33 (triplicate ratio of corresponding sides). Auxiliary magnitudes E, F, G, H are constructed as third/fourth proportionals and are also pure magnitudes. In the converse, a solid SE similar to SC is constructed on E by 11.27. No vertices, edges, faces, angles, or spatial positions are ever specified. The entire proof operates through proportion theory (Book 5) applied to the ratio results of 11.33. There are no spatial configuration claims that could conflict.
pass_reason: The proof is a proportion/ratio argument throughout. Parallelepipedal solids appear but are treated purely through their ratio properties via 11.33 (triplicate ratio) and 11.27 (construction of similar solids). No spatial configuration claims are made — no point positions, angle decompositions, betweenness claims, plane memberships, or inside/outside assertions. All claims (solid similarity, ratio relationships, solid equality) are mutually consistent.
